This indicates a potential pathway where Oxtriphylline influences Pde3a via Adora2a and Dyphylline. The lowest common ancestor of these interactions is Oxtriphylline and Dyphylline, suggesting a shared regulatory role in the pathway. The binding scores indicate a moderate level of interaction, suggesting that Oxtriphylline may modulate Pde3a activity through these intermediaries. The evidence supports a mechanistic link between Oxtriphylline and Pde3a, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
